newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian military spurn contact with Albania rebels.
newsitem.headline: Italian military spurn contact with Albania rebels.

text.p: The commander of the Italian-led multinational security mission in distressed Albania on Wednesday ruled out direct contacts with rebel committees that control much of the south.
"Our contacts will be with the recognised central and local government authorities," General Luciano Forlani, who leads an eight-nation U.N.-approved force, told a news conference.
"We will ask the Tirana government to tell us who our contacts should be in areas where we go," he added.

He also said that the multinational force, which will eventually number 6,000 troops, was not planning to conduct joint patrols with the Albanian police. About two thirds of the force have already arrived in Albania.

The troops are protecting deliveries of humanitarian aid to the poor who have suffered most in weeks of chaos since an armed insurrection triggered by the failure of bogus investment schemes. At least 300 people have been killed in the violence.
Rebel committees, which reject the authority of President Sali Berisha, control much of the south. They say Berisha, a northerner, is responsible for the failure of the savings schemes.

Asked whether the Italian navy was to blame for its flagship getting stuck on a sandbank off the southern rebel-held port of Vlore, Forlani said: "Accidents happen. There are accidents on the ground, in the sea, in the air."
He added: "There was a strong sirocco wind, which came up rapidly, with unusual force, and made the ship go forward."
Four tugs pulled the Vittorio Veneto free early on Wednesday after it lay stuck for more than a day.
Italian navy officials said they had begun an internal investigation into the incident.
Albania's long-exiled King Leka I is planning a trip to Vlore on Thursday, a spokesman for the monarchist party said.
"I am positive that the people of Vlore will give Leka a warm welcome," Guri Durollari, chairman of the Legality Movement Party, told reporters.
He said Leka, who returned from exile in South Africa this month to urge the restoration of the monarchy, would meet Vlore residents but did not plan to contact the rebel committee.
Leka, 58, would take no special security measures in the violence-stricken city, Durollari said.
"We will be meeting our brothers and sisters, so there is no need to be worried," he said.
Last Sunday Leka paid a triumphal visit to his ancestral village north of Tirana. More than 5,000 people turned out to welcome him.
Leka was two days old when his father, King Zog, fled with his family in 1939 ahead of invading Italian fascists.
In the western port of Durres, soldiers from the multinational force continued to arrive. About 520 Greek troops landed on two tank-landing ships, officials said.
The Greek navy vessels Samos and Chios, which carried the troops as well as 92 tanks and armoured vehicles, arrived from the northern Greek port of Salonika.
The first Austrian troops to join the force left for Albania from their barracks just outside Vienna.
The 74 soldiers, part of Austria's 115-strong contribution to the mission, were expected to take a ferry from the Italian port of Brindisi to the Albanian port of Durres.
The troops will be stationed in Tirana where they will be responsible for protecting the headquarters of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
